correctness.rationale: The nine rational points are the transverse (3,3) complete intersection V(H,G); Cayley–Bacharach forces any cubic through eight through the ninth. Every member of the cubic pencil other than H factors into three rational lines, excluding an integral eight-point cubic. The displayed C0 is smooth by simultaneous gradient equations and contains exactly seven H(F4) points. An exhaustive coefficient-projective census checks 349525 cubics; a separate nullspace census checks the 36 omitted pairs and all 16 exact-seven members per pair, finding five without rational line factors per pair. High rational point counts rule out both geometric reducibility and singularity. Bézout, no degree-two points on H, and exact tangent comparison prove the indicated (3,1^6)/(2^2,1^5) contact divisors. Both supplied verifier programs passed.
